seo.title: Quant — automated trading operator for MOEX
seo.description: Quant analyses the market, checks the strategy against written rules, measures confidence, limits risk and executes through your broker account. It starts in the sandbox.
seo.ogTitle: The market makes noise. Quant turns it into a decision.
seo.ogDescription: Automated trading operator for MOEX. Closed testing.

hero.subline: A trading operator for MOEX. The rules are written in advance, risk is checked before the order, and the last word stays yours.

audience.heading: One Quant. Different levels of control.
audience.lead: It is the same product throughout. What changes is how much you want to see, and how much you want to decide yourself.
audience.card1Body: Start in the sandbox: the same signals and the same decision path, without real money. You can confirm every trade by hand until you trust the system.
audience.card2Body: The rules are written down and readable, the market regime is classified, confidence is measured from closed trades, and risk is checked before entry. We publish frozen strategies alongside the working ones.
audience.card3Title: If you are a partner or developer
audience.card3Body: Telegram and the dashboard read the same state from one shared data layer. Keys are encrypted, actions are logged, and withdrawal permissions are never requested — there is no such method in the broker interface at all.
audience.card4Body: No win rate, no profit factor, no return — there is not a single result figure on this site. Frozen strategies sit alongside the working ones, and there is no automatic kill switch, which we say plainly.

foundation.heading: What this rests on
foundation.lead: Three principles the product is built on. They are ordered: each one only means anything if you accept the one before it.

telegram.lead: Not a notification feed and not a simplified copy: a second interface onto the same state, the same engine and the same database.

safety.heading: Quant works with your account. Here are the boundaries.
safety.lead: The constraints below are properties of the code, not promises. Where a constraint is incomplete, we say so directly.
safety.item1Body: The broker interface Quant uses has no withdraw or transfer method. Not “disabled by configuration” — the code does not exist. Withdrawal permissions are not needed to connect.
safety.item2Body: Share per position, daily loss, number of open positions and the ATR stop are all checked before the broker is called. Fail one and the order is never sent.
safety.item3Body: The broker client starts in sandbox mode. Moving to real money is a separate, deliberate step, not a default.
safety.item4Body: The engine can be paused and stopped from Telegram and from the dashboard. Drawdown is monitored and sends an alert, but does not halt trading by itself: there is no automatic kill switch.
safety.item5Body: Broker keys are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) in an owner-only file — encryption is switched on by a master key at deployment. Credential changes are written to an audit log, and the keys themselves can be revoked on the broker side at any time.
safety.item6Body: Confidence in a strategy stays within 0.05–0.95 and never becomes certainty. A signal below 0.20 is recorded but not executed.

faq.heading: Questions
faq.a1: No — not neural networks, and not language models. There is not a single ML library in the project. The rules are written in advance and readable, and “confidence” is a smoothed mean of win rate, profit factor and expectancy, updated after each closed trade.
faq.q2: Can I start without risking capital?
faq.a2: Yes. The sandbox runs the same decision path as live, but fills against simulated prices. No real money is involved until you switch the mode yourself.
faq.a3: A mode where signals, rules and risk checks all run for real, but execution is simulated: a trade fills at the observed price with commission and slippage applied. It is a way to see how the system behaves before trusting it with an account.
faq.a4: The decision is assembled from checks: the rules produce a score, the confidence gate compares it against a floor, the risk manager sizes the position and checks the limits. Any one of them can stop the trade. You set the limits, and you can stop the engine at any point.
faq.a5: Yes. A manual order goes through two steps, showing every parameter before it is sent. A signal card in Telegram executes in the sandbox with one button.
faq.a6: In an encrypted vault (AES-256-GCM) readable only by the file's owner; changes are written to an audit log. Encryption is switched on by a master key — if it is not set at deployment, keys stay in a plain .env, and that must be fixed before any live run.
faq.a7: No. The broker interface Quant uses has no withdraw or transfer method at all — only orders, cancellation and reading account state. Withdrawal permissions are not required when connecting keys.
faq.a8: No. Guaranteed returns do not exist and we do not promise them. That is why there is not a single performance figure on this site: trading carries the risk of losing capital.
faq.a9: Today, MOEX through T-Invest. Bybit is connected for reading balances and positions only; there are no crypto strategies in the system yet. Finam is planned but not implemented.
faq.a10: Live is opened by hand, and only after the sandbox, configured risk limits and confirmed consent. We do not move anyone to live on payment — and payment is not connected at all right now.

finalCta.heading: Start in the sandbox. Move to live when you are ready.
